arxiv-2011-07444.title: Performance Analysis for the CMSA/CA Protocol in UAV-based IoT network
arxiv-2011-07444.creator: Xianzhen Guo, Bin Li, Kebang Liu
arxiv-2011-07444.description: Abstract UAV-based base station (UBS) has played an important role in the air-ground integration network due to its high flexibility and nice air-ground wireless channels. Especially in Internet of Things (IoT) services, UBS can provide an efficient way for data collection from the IoT devices.

arxiv-2012-11181.title: Escaping an Infinitude of Lions
arxiv-2012-11181.creator: Mikkel Abrahamsen, Jacob HolmEva Rotenberg, Christian Wulff-Nilsen
arxiv-2012-11181.description: Abstract We consider the following game played in the Euclidean plane: There is any countable set of unit speed lions and one fast man who can run with speed 1 + ε 1+\varepsilon for some value ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 . Can the man survive? We answer the question in the affirmative for any ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 .

arxiv-2103-05792.title: Equi-Joins over Encrypted Data for Series of Queries
arxiv-2103-05792.creator: Masoumeh Shafieinejad, Suraj Gupta, Jin Yang Liu, Koray Karabina, Florian Kerschbaum
arxiv-2103-05792.description: Abstract . Encryption provides a method to protect data outsourced to a DBMS provider, e.g., in the cloud. However, performing database operations over encrypted data requires specialized encryption schemes that carefully balance security and performance. In this paper, we present a new encryption scheme that can efficiently perform equi-joins over encrypted data with better security than the state-of-the-art.

arxiv-2107-03563.title: The performance of IHEP-NDL LGAD sensors after neutron irradiation
arxiv-2107-03563.creator: Gregor Kramberger
arxiv-2107-03563.description: Abstract The performances of Low Gain Avalanche diode (LGAD) sensors from a neutron irradiation campaign with fluences of 0.8 × 10 15 0.8\text{\,}\times\mathrm{1}\mathrm{0}^{15} , 1.5 × 10 15 1.5\text{\,}\times\mathrm{1}\mathrm{0}^{15} and 2.5 × 10 15 ​ n e ​ q / cm 2 2.5\text{\,}\times\mathrm{1}\mathrm{0}^{15}~\mathrm{n}_{eq}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{c}\mathrm{m}^{2} are reported in this article.

arxiv-2203-09250.title: Symmetry-Based Representations for Artificial and Biological General Intelligence
arxiv-2203-09250.creator: Irina Higgins, Sébastien Racanière, Danilo Rezende
arxiv-2203-09250.description: Abstract Biological intelligence is remarkable in its ability to produce complex behaviour in many diverse situations through data efficient, generalisable and transferable skill acquisition. It is believed that learning “good” sensory representations is important for enabling this, however there is little agreement as to what a good representation should look like.

arxiv-2210-07458.title: Semiclassical geometrodynamics of homogeneous cosmology
arxiv-2210-07458.creator: Viqar Husain, Muhammad Muzammil
arxiv-2210-07458.description: Abstract We study the classical-quantum (CQ) hybrid dynamics of homogeneous cosmology from a Hamiltonian perspective where the classical gravitational phase space variables and matter state evolve self-consistently with full backreaction. We compare numerically the classical and CQ dynamics for isotropic and anisotropic models, including quantum scalar-field induced corrections to the Kasner exponents.

arxiv-2306-11350.title: Nonclassical radiation from a nonlinear oscillator driven solely by classical 1 / f 1/f noise
arxiv-2306-11350.creator: Archak Purkayastha, Klaus Mølmer
arxiv-2306-11350.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Archak Purkayastha, Klaus Mølmer. Low-frequency classical 1 / f 1/f -noise and quantum noise from low-temperature phonon modes are ubiquitous across various experimental platforms, and are usually considered a hindrance for quantum technological applications. Here we show that the simultaneous action of classical 1 / f 1/f noise and a low-temperature phonon bath on a nonlinear oscillator can result in the generation of nonclassical antibunched radiation without the need for any additional drive.

arxiv-2401-09724.title: Predicting Viral Rumors and Vulnerable Users with Graph-based Neural Multi-task Learning for Infodemic Surveillance
arxiv-2401-09724.creator: Xuan Zhang, Wei Gao
arxiv-2401-09724.description: Abstract In the age of the infodemic, it is crucial to have tools for effectively monitoring the spread of rampant rumors that can quickly go viral, as well as identifying vulnerable users who may be more susceptible to spreading such misinformation.

arxiv-2402-15692.title: Designing for Human Operations on the Moon: Challenges and Opportunities of Navigational HUD Interfaces Conference: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; May 11–16, 2024; Honolulu, HI, USA Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI
arxiv-2402-15692.creator: Leonie Bensch, Tommy Nilsson, Jan Wulkop, Paul de Medeiros, Nicolas Daniel Herzberger, Michael Preutenborbeck, Andreas Gerndt, Frank Flemisch, Florian Dufresne, Georgia Albuquerque, Aidan Cowley
arxiv-2402-15692.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Leonie Bensch, Tommy Nilsson, Jan Wulkop, Paul de Medeiros, Nicolas Daniel Herzberger, Michael Preutenborbeck, Andreas Gerndt, Frank Flemisch, Florian Dufresne, Georgia Albuquerque, Aidan Cowley. Future crewed missions to the Moon will face significant environmental and operational challenges, posing risks to the safety and performance of astronauts navigating its inhospitable surface.

arxiv-2404-16633.title: Self-Balanced R-CNN for Instance Segmentation
arxiv-2404-16633.creator: Leonardo Rossi, Akbar Karimi, Andrea Prati
arxiv-2404-16633.description: Abstract Current state-of-the-art two-stage models on instance segmentation task suffer from several types of imbalances. In this paper, we address the Intersection over the Union (IoU) distribution imbalance of positive input Regions of Interest (RoIs) during the training of the second stage.

arxiv-2407-06059.title: LaFAM: Unsupervised Feature Attribution with Label-free Activation Maps
arxiv-2407-06059.creator: Aray Karjauv, Sahin Albayrak
arxiv-2407-06059.description: Abstract Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are known for their ability to learn hierarchical structures, naturally developing detectors for objects, and semantic concepts within their deeper layers. Activation maps (AMs) reveal these saliency regions, which are crucial for many Explainable AI (XAI) methods. However, the direct exploitation of raw AMs in CNNs for feature attribution remains underexplored in literature.

arxiv-2502-13581.title: ActionPiece: Contextually Tokenizing Action Sequences for Generative Recommendation
arxiv-2502-13581.creator: Yupeng Hou, Jianmo Ni, Zhankui He, Noveen Sachdeva, Wang-Cheng Kang, Ed H. Chi, Julian McAuley, Derek Zhiyuan Cheng
arxiv-2502-13581.description: Abstract Generative recommendation (GR) is an emerging paradigm where user actions are tokenized into discrete token patterns and autoregressively generated as predictions. However, existing GR models tokenize each action independently, assigning the same fixed tokens to identical actions across all sequences without considering contextual relationships.

arxiv-2503-10916.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, IV. Resilience of the graph calculus in the dimensional shift d ↦ d + 1 d\mapsto d+1
arxiv-2503-10916.creator: Mollie S. Jagoe Brown, Arthemy V. Kiselev
arxiv-2503-10916.description: Abstract We examine whether the Kontsevich flows P ˙ = Q d γ ​ ( P ) \dot{P}=Q^{\gamma}_{d}(P) of Nambu–Poisson structures P P on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} are Poisson coboundaries, for γ \gamma some suitable cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex.

arxiv-2506-05164.title: Towards the Target and Not Beyond: 2D vs 3D Visual Aids in MR-Based Neurosurgical Simulation
arxiv-2506-05164.creator: Pasquale Cascarano, Andrea Loretti, Matteo Martinoni, Luca Zanuttini, Alessio Di Pasquale, Gustavo Marfia
arxiv-2506-05164.description: Abstract Neurosurgery increasingly uses Mixed Reality (MR) technologies for intraoperative assistance. The greatest challenge in this area is mentally reconstructing complex 3D anatomical structures from 2D slices with millimetric precision, which is required in procedures like External Ventricular Drain (EVD) placement.

arxiv-2512-16079.title: Linear dimension of group actions
arxiv-2512-16079.creator: Alice Devillers, Michael Giudici, Daniel R. Hawtin, Lukas Klawuhn, Luke Morgan
arxiv-2512-16079.description: Abstract . Two fundamental ways to represent a group are as permutations and as matrices. In this paper, we study linear representations of groups that intertwine with a permutation representation. Recently, D’Alconzo and Di Scala [ 8 ] investigated how small the matrices in such a linear representation can be.

arxiv-2601-01692.title: Enhanced Multi-model Online Conformal Prediction Thanks: Work in the paper is supported by NSF EECS 2207457, NSF ECCS 2412484 and NSF ECCS 2442964.
arxiv-2601-01692.creator: Erfan Hajihashemi, Yanning Shen
arxiv-2601-01692.description: Abstract Conformal prediction is a framework for uncertainty quantification that constructs prediction sets for previously unseen data, guaranteeing coverage of the true label with a specified probability. However, the efficiency of these prediction sets, measured by their size, depends on the choice of the underlying learning model.

plos-pone-0004627.creator: Karunya K. Kandimalla, Olenych G. Scott, Smita Fulzele et al.
plos-pone-0004627.description: PLOS ONE research article. Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by significant neurodegeneration in the cortex and hippocampus; intraneuronal tangles of hyperphosphorylated tau protein; and accumulation of β-amyloid (Aβ) proteins 40 and 42 in the brain parenchyma as well as in the cerebral vasculature

pmc-10548624.title: Exploring the translational potential of PLGA nanoparticles for intra-articular rapamycin delivery in osteoarthritis therapy
pmc-10548624.creator: Jian-Chao Ma, Tingting Luo, Binyang Feng, Zicheng Huang, Yiqing Zhang, Hanqing Huang, Xiao Yang, Jing Wen, Xiaochun Bai, Zhong-Kai Cui
pmc-10548624.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent joint disease that affects all the tissues within the joint and currently lacks disease-modifying treatments in clinical practice. Despite the potential of rapamycin for OA disease alleviation, its clinical application is hindered by the challenge of achieving therapeutic concentrations, which necessitates multiple injections per week.

pmc-11311056.title: Impact of Personality Trait Interactions on Foraging and Growth in Native and Invasive Turtles
pmc-11311056.creator: Lin Gan, Shufang Zhang, Ruyi Zeng, Tianyi Shen, Liu Tian, Hao Yu, Ke Hua, Yue Wang
pmc-11311056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryAnimal personalities could affect the behavior and physiology of both native and invasive species during biological invasion. However, little is known about the personality interaction effects on foraging behavior and growth between native and invasive species. We used the red-eared slider turtle and Chinese pond turtle as models to investigate how personality interactions effect the foraging behavior and growth of both these turtle species. The results showed that the foraging behavior of M.

pmc-11392699.title: Incidence of hypothermia in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy in Siriraj Hospital in Siriraj Hospital, Thailand
pmc-11392699.creator: Thonnarat Pornsirirat, Nualnapa Kasemvilawan, Patcharavalia Pattanacharoenwong, Saisunee Arpibanwana, Hatairat Kondon, Thummaporn Naorungroj
pmc-11392699.description: BackgroundHypothermia is a relatively common complication in patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). However, few studies have reported the factors associated with hypothermia.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was performed in five intensive care units (ICUs) to evaluate the incidence of hypothermia and the predictive factors for developing hypothermia during CRRT, with hypothermia defined as a time-weighted average temperature <36 °C.

pmc-11425591.title: Dehumanizing air travel: a scoping review on accessibility and inclusion of people with disabilities in international airports
pmc-11425591.creator: David Gotti, Ernesto Morales, François Routhier, Jonathan Riendeau, Ahmed Hadj Hassen
pmc-11425591.description: IntroductionWorldwide, one in six individuals live with a disability. Many people continue to experience disabling situations, particularly when travelling. Travel can be an important part of the lives of many people, including people with disabilities. Barriers to accessing air travel can lead to a reluctance to travel for these potential passengers.

pmc-11714752.title: Tau‐PET imaging in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and relationship with biomarkers and clinical markers
pmc-11714752.creator: Roxane Dilcher, Charles B Malpas, Terence J O'Brien, Lucy Vivash
pmc-11714752.description: BackgroundIdentifying biomarkers for primary tau pathologies like Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) is crucial for diagnosis and treatment development. The novel positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracer 18F‐PI‐2620 shows promise in detecting tau protein in PSP and this study investigates its correlation with clinical markers.

pmc-12413081.title: What drives the demand for drought-resilient sorghum varieties? Evidence from moisture-stressed areas in Ethiopia
pmc-12413081.creator: Mekonnen Sime, Dereje Mersha, Mesay Yami
pmc-12413081.description: Sorghum is one of the critical food security crops, particularly in moisture-stressed areas of Ethiopia. However, in the absence of a well-organized formal seed system, public research institutions have continued to promote and disseminate improved sorghum varieties to encourage adoption.

pmc-12470019.title: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis: Comprehensive Review and Exploration of the Dual Potential of Cyclodextrins in Therapeutic Optimization
pmc-12470019.creator: Filipa Mascarenhas-Melo, Bruna Martins, Inês Monteiro, Alka Lohani, Karolline Krambeck, Ligia Petrica
pmc-12470019.description: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a histopathological pattern of segmental glomerulosclerosis that arises from diverse primary and secondary causes. Primary (idiopathic) FSGS is rare and is often linked to intrinsic podocyte injury, while secondary forms are more prevalent and may reflect adaptative, toxic, genetic, or viral etiologies.

pmc-12653472.title: Endothelial Cells Differentiated from Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Form Aligned Network Structures in Engineered Neural Tissue
pmc-12653472.creator: Poppy O. Smith, Parmjit Jat, James B. Phillips
pmc-12653472.description: Background/Objectives: Endothelial cells play a key role in peripheral nerve regeneration, forming aligned vasculature which bridges the gap in the injured nerve tissue and guides the regrowing tissue. This work aimed to mimic key features of this aligned vasculature by differentiating endothelial cells from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and incorporating them into engineered neural tissue (EngNT).

pmc-12654086.title: Assessing the Influence of Proton Pump Inhibitors on Clinical Outcomes in Hormone Receptor-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer Patients Receiving CDK4/6 Inhibitors: Evidence from a Ribociclib-Dominant Cohort
pmc-12654086.creator: Enes Erul, Nejat Emre Öksüz, Erman Akkus, Pınar Kubilay Tolunay, Elif Berna Köksoy, Hatime Arzu Yasar
pmc-12654086.description: Background and Objectives: Endocrine therapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibitors are widely recognized as the standard first-line approach for treating hormone receptor-positive HER2-negative (HR+/HER2−) metastatic breast cancer (mBC). Nonetheless, potential pharmacokinetic interactions—particularly with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)—have raised concerns about reduced drug bioavailability and compromised therapeutic efficacy.

pmc-12752216.title: Exploring a mutation-based signature to predict the benefits of immune checkpoint inhibitors in oncogene-addicted subsets of non-small cell lung cancer: a retrospective study
pmc-12752216.creator: Jing Huang, Jinsong Lei, Baoyou Xiao, Wenyan Kang, Zhilin Sui, Youjun Deng, Ran Jia, Chujian Huang, Songhua Cai
pmc-12752216.description: BackgroundDespite the effectiveness of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in cancer treatment, oncogene-addicted subsets of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) typically derive limited benefits. Herein, we established and evaluated a mutation-based signature to predict ICB efficacy in patients with both non-mutant and oncogene-mutant NSCLC.

pmc-13084699.title: Improved red blood cell storage quality of blood from donors carrying the hypermorphic PIMT I120 variant
pmc-13084699.creator: Shaun Bevers, Aaron V. Issaian, Ariel Hay, Gregory R. Keele, Monika Dzieciatkowska, Julie A. Reisz, Zachary B. Haiman, Travis Nemkov, Daniel Stephenson, Amy L. Moore, Xutao Deng, Mars Stone, Kirk C. Hansen, Steve Kleinman, Philip J. Norris, Michael P. Busch, Bernhard O. Palsson, Nareg H. Roubinian,
pmc-13084699.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Protein‐l‐isoaspartate O‐methyltransferase (PIMT), encoded by PCMT1, is a repair enzyme that corrects isoaspartyl lesions, preserving protein structure and function. While indispensable for neuronal integrity, its role in red blood cells (RBCs) and transfusion outcomes is incompletely understood. Here, we show that novel erythroid‐specific Pcmt1 knockout mice display profound remodeling of one‐carbon metabolism, accumulation of repair intermediates, and destabilization of glycolytic and cytoskeletal proteins, yet maintain lower lipid peroxidation and normal post‐transfusion recovery.

pmc-13118936.title: Hemolytic Activity of Vaginal Candida albicans Isolates and Antifungal Effects of Quinalizarin with Hemolysis Modulation
pmc-13118936.creator: Monika Janeczko, Elżbieta Kochanowicz
pmc-13118936.description: This study evaluated the hemolytic activity of Candida albicans isolates from the female reproductive tract and investigated the in vitro effects of quinalizarin on fungal growth, hemolysis, and ECE1 expression. Ninety-four clinical C. albicans isolates and three ATCC reference strains were analyzed. Hemolytic activity was quantified in culture supernatants and normalized per 107 cells.

pmc-13188717.title: Winning beyond scoring: an explainable machine learning framework for identifying key performance indicators in the Chinese Basketball Association
pmc-13188717.creator: Rui Dong, Yingkang Peng, Qing Liu, Miguel-Angel Gómez-Ruano, Shaoliang Zhang, Xiao Xu, Bin Yang, Hongyou Liu
pmc-13188717.description: BackgroundUnderstanding why teams win in professional basketball requires more than examining isolated statistics. Performance adapts under changing competitive constraints, and key performance indicators (KPIs) must therefore be interpreted within context. This study aimed to develop an explainable, multi-model machine learning (ML) framework to identify score-line dependent KPIs associated with winning outcomes in the Chinese Basketball Association (CBA).

pmc-13336567.title: Fulminant Postoperative Peritonitis Following Cocaine Packet Rupture in a Body Packer

pmc-13554194.title: Cardiac-derived extracellular vesicles carrying miR-4433b-3p accelerate cognitive decline and brain aging by suppressing TP53INP2-mediated neuronal autophagy in mice
pmc-13554194.creator: Qian Cheng, Zhikang Cui, Shuyi Yu, Guixia Li, Hang Chen, Qian Yu, Jialin Han, Shuang Wu, Yan Jin, Yunshan Wang, Ming Li, Zhiming Lu
pmc-13554194.description: Brain aging is not an independent process, yet how systemic aging drives neural decline remains unclear. Here, we identified a circulating miR-4433b-3p, packaged within extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a trans-organ effector bridging cardiac aging with central nervous system (CNS) decline.

pmc-13674092.title: Robotic tricuspid valve repair for infective endocarditis with leaflet perforation and severe tricuspid regurgitation
pmc-13674092.creator: Shaan Asif, George Comas, Richard Bloomingdale, Rakesh M. Suri
pmc-13674092.description: tricuspid endocarditis. Central Message Robotic tricuspid valve repair is a feasible minimally invasive option for selected patients with tricuspid-valve endocarditis, enabling complete debridement while preserving the native valve. The risk of tricuspid-valve infective endocarditis (TVIE) is strongly associated with intravenous drug use and Staphylococcus aureus infection.
